mechanism.name: Pointwise conditional-mean query at a fixed interior design point in the Hall and Horowitz (2013) univariate smooth regression design

generation_equations.label: 1. Observed design
generation_equations.expression: X_i iid Uniform(-1,1). Source support -1..1; one scalar covariate per row.

generation_equations.label: 2. Mean function
generation_equations.expression: g1(x)=x+5*exp(-50*x^2)/sqrt(2*pi); g2(x)=sin(3*pi*x/2)/(1+18*x^2*(sgn(x)+1)); g3(x)=sin(pi*x/2)/(1+2*x^2*(sgn(x)+1)). Deterministic; sgn(x)=-1/0/1 for x<0/=0/>0. All coefficients are from the source unnumbered functions.

generation_equations.label: 3. Regression error
generation_equations.expression: epsilon_i iid N(0,sigma^2), independent of X; registered pairs are (g1,sigma=1),(g2,0.5),(g3,0.2). sigma is a standard deviation, not a variance; the source has a full 3-by-3 design.

generation_equations.label: 4. Observed response
generation_equations.expression: Y_i=g_j(X_i)+epsilon_i; return X,Y. No extra noise, latent mean or oracle column.

sampling.unit: One scalar covariate/outcome pair (X_i, Y_i), one observation per independent unit
sampling.dependence: iid across i with no within-cluster correlation; X_i is drawn independently of epsilon_i, so observations share nothing beyond the fixed DGP parameters

assumptions: Independent and identically distributed pairs (X_i, Y_i); no clustering, serial dependence, spatial or network interference is present.
X_i is drawn uniformly on [-1,1], so its density is bounded away from zero at every interior query point used here and local smoothing has design points on both sides of x0.
epsilon_i ~ N(0, sigma^2) is independent of X_i and additive, so no correction for heteroskedasticity, measurement error or endogenous regressors is required to identify E[Y | X = x0].
g_j is bounded on [-1,1] and smooth enough for the local-polynomial regularity assumed in Section 2 of the source; g2 and g3 are continuous at x = 0 where the sign convention switches.

The query point x0 is fixed interior to the support and chosen before seeing data; pointwise verification at one or several x0 does not establish simultaneous coverage over the source evaluation interval [-0.9, 0.9].
This is a non-causal regression target: no intervention, exposure, exchangeability or counterfactual consistency assumption is claimed.

properties.notes: The single covariate X is the only input, so dimension = effective_dimension = 1 and high_dimensional is false relative to the source sample sizes n = 100, 200, 400. interactions is false: the mean depends on X through one univariate function with no product term between covariates. nonlinear is true for two explicit reasons: g1 adds a narrow Gaussian spike 5*phi(10x) = 5*exp(-50x^2)/sqrt(2*pi) (effective bandwidth 0.1) to a linear trend, and g2/g3 are sign-split rational sine functions whose denominator is 1 for x<0 (sgn(x)+1=0); at x=0 that factor equals 1 but x^2=0, so the denominator remains 1. For x > 0 the denominator is 1 + 2*a*x^2 with a = 18 (g2) and a = 2 (g3). The observed columns are only X and Y; the noise draw is not exported.

estimand.name: m(x0) = E[Y | X = x0] = g_j(x0)
estimand.definition: The value of the conditional mean function at one fixed interior design point x0 specified per scenario, in the superpopulation defined by the declared regression model with X uniform on [-1,1] and additive N(0, sigma^2) noise. This is a pointwise scalar query, not a simultaneous confidence band and not a coverage claim over any interval.

truth.expression: The value of the conditional mean function at one fixed interior design point x0 specified per scenario, in the superpopulation defined by the declared regression model with X uniform on [-1,1] and additive N(0, sigma^2) noise. This is a pointwise scalar query, not a simultaneous confidence band and not a coverage claim over any interval.
truth.derivation: Closed-form substitution of the scenario query point into g_j, with phi(10x) = exp(-50x^2)/sqrt(2*pi) evaluated directly and sgn(x) applied branch-wise; a single elementary evaluation, so the reported error is a floating-point rounding allowance rather than a quadrature or Monte Carlo error estimate. Reported estimated_error is 1e-12.
